Batcave for iPhone - Xcode project
==================================

You need: a Mac with Xcode 26 or newer (free from the Mac App Store).
No Node, npm or Terminal needed: the app's screens are already bundled in
ios/App/App/public.

See it in the iPhone Simulator (no Apple account needed)
1. Double-click ios/App/App.xcodeproj. Xcode opens it. The first open
   downloads the Capacitor Swift package (about a minute; watch the
   progress bar at the top).
2. At the top of the Xcode window, click the device menu next to "App"
   and pick any iPhone simulator, for example "iPhone 17".
3. Press the Run button (the triangle), or Command-R.
4. The app opens on "Connect to your Batcave server". Type your server
   address, for example https://your-app.up.railway.app, and the access
   key if your server sets BATCAVE_ACCESS_KEY. Both stay on the device.
   If the screen shows "Try the demo", that opens the sample-data demo
   instead (simulated market, labelled SAMPLE DATA on every screen).

Run it on your own iPhone
5. Click "App" in the left sidebar, then the App target, then
   Signing & Capabilities. Set Team to your Apple Account (the free
   Personal Team works). If Xcode says the bundle identifier is taken,
   change com.batcave.terminal to something unique, such as
   com.yourname.batcave.
6. Plug in the iPhone, pick it as the run destination and press Run.
   On the phone: Settings > General > VPN & Device Management > trust
   your developer certificate; turn on Developer Mode if asked.
   Apps signed with a free Personal Team expire after 7 days; press Run
   again to reinstall.

What the app is
- A native shell around the Batcave web UI. All data, math and Schwab
  tokens stay on your server. The app holds no Schwab keys.
- Connect Schwab from the website or from Settings in the app; the login
  opens in Safari and the server stores the tokens.
